Profile likelihood on a grid of conductance parameters

Source: R/radish_grid.R
terradish_grid.Rd

Calculates the profile likelihood of a parameterized conductance surface across a grid of parameter values (that is, the nuisance parameters are optimized at each point on the grid).

Usage

terradish_grid(
  theta,
  formula,
  data,
  conductance_model = loglinear_conductance,
  measurement_model = mlpe,
  nu = NULL,
  nonnegative = TRUE,
  conductance = TRUE,
  covariance = FALSE,
  cores = 1L,
  approximation = "none",
  approximation_control = NULL
)

Arguments

theta

A matrix of dimension (grid size) x (number of parameters)

formula

A formula with the name of a response matrix compatible with the selected measurement model on the left-hand side, and covariates used to create data on the right-hand side.

data

An object of class terradish_graph (see conductance_surface)

conductance_model

A function of class terradish_conductance_model_factory (see terradish_conductance_model_factory)

measurement_model

A function of class terradish_measurement_model (see terradish_measurement_model)

nu

Effective Wishart degrees of freedom passed to measurement models that require it. This is a user-supplied effective-information parameter, not the marker count. Report sensitivity to plausible values; see wishart_covariance.

nonnegative

Force regression-like measurement_model to have nonnegative slope?

conductance

Retained for backward compatibility. Only conductance = TRUE is currently implemented.

covariance

If TRUE, additionally return (a submatrix of) the generalized inverse of graph Laplacian across the grid

cores

Number of worker processes to use. 1 evaluates the grid serially.

approximation

Only "none" is supported; every grid point uses the full graph and focal set.

approximation_control

Reserved for compatibility; unused.

Value

A list of class c("terradish_grid", "radish_grid"), with one entry per row of theta:

theta

Data frame of the evaluated conductance coefficients (log conductance per unit of each covariate).

loglik

Numeric vector of profile log-likelihoods, with nuisance parameters optimized at each grid point. Larger values indicate better fit, and differences between grid points are on the log-likelihood scale.

phi

Matrix of optimized nuisance parameters, one column per grid point, on the measurement model's internal scale.

covariance

When covariance = TRUE, a focal-site by focal-site by grid-point array of graph covariance (the generalized inverse of the graph Laplacian); otherwise NULL.

approximation

Record of the approximation setting (always "none").

See also

terradish for the optimizer and terradish_distance for resistance distances on the same kind of grid.

Other model fitting: conductance(), terradish(), terradish_algorithm(), terradish_distance(), terradish_methods

Examples

# \donttest{
library(terra)

data(melip)
covariates <- c(terra::unwrap(melip.altitude),
                terra::unwrap(melip.forestcover))
coords <- terra::unwrap(melip.coords)
names(covariates) <- c("altitude", "forestcover")
# Coarsened so the example runs quickly; name layers, then scale.
covariates <- scale_covariates(terra::aggregate(covariates, fact = 3,
                                                na.rm = TRUE))
# Keep one site per raster cell (some melip sites share a cell).
keep <- !duplicated(terra::cellFromXY(covariates, terra::crds(coords)))
Fst <- melip.Fst[keep, keep]
surface <- conductance_surface(covariates, coords[keep])

fit_mlpe <- terradish(Fst ~ altitude + forestcover, data = surface,
                      measurement_model = mlpe)

theta <- as.matrix(expand.grid(forestcover = seq(-0.5, 0.5, length.out = 3),
                               altitude = seq(-0.5, 0.5, length.out = 3)))

grid <- terradish_grid(theta, Fst ~ forestcover + altitude, surface,
                       measurement_model = mlpe)

# Profile log-likelihood at each grid point; the maximum should lie near
# the fitted coefficients.
cbind(grid$theta, loglik = grid$loglik)
#>   forestcover altitude   loglik
#> 1        -0.5     -0.5 1468.833
#> 2         0.0     -0.5 1492.091
#> 3         0.5     -0.5 1485.862
#> 4        -0.5      0.0 1403.162
#> 5         0.0      0.0 1443.254
#> 6         0.5      0.0 1460.622
#> 7        -0.5      0.5 1344.748
#> 8         0.0      0.5 1384.486
#> 9         0.5      0.5 1401.381
coef(fit_mlpe)
#>    altitude forestcover 
#> -0.79206795 -0.09612631 
# }
